references.text: Moses' staff is first introduced as a tool for God's signs and wonders
Moses stretches out his staff over the waters of Egypt, turning the water into blood
Fulfillment of God's command - Moses stretches out his hand and the sea parts
The Israelites walked on dry ground in the middle of the sea, with water as a wall on both sides
Moses' song of praise describes how the waters stood up like a heap and the deep froze solid
Joshua reminds the people how the Lord dried up the Sea of Reeds before them
The psalmist praises God who turned the sea into dry land
The psalmist recounts how God split the sea and led the people through it
The Lord threatened the Sea of Reeds until it became dry, and led the people through the deep as through a desert
Praise to God who split the Sea of Reeds and led Israel through
Isaiah refers to God who dried up the sea and made the depths of the sea a way for the redeemed
Isaiah reminds how God's glorious arm led the people through the deep
The letter to the Hebrews notes that by faith the Israelites passed through the Red Sea as on dry land
Paul writes that all their fathers passed through the sea and were baptized into Moses in the cloud and in the sea
Direct continuation of the same event: From command to fulfillment.
Thematic connection through the motif of 'Moses' staff' as an instrument of God's power across the events of the wilderness journey.
Prophetic allusion to the Exodus as a cosmic display of power ('split the earth with rivers').
Contrast parallel: The same gestures and tools lead to judgment (blood) in Egypt, but deliverance (dry ground) for Israel.
